content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Ceftaroline, sold under the brand name Teflaro, is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections. It is administered by injection into a vein, typically every 8 or 12 hours, as directed by your doctor. The dosage depends on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. For optimal results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, as well as nausea or diarrhea. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using ceftaroline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ceftaroline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ceftaroline may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as Coombs' tests or urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as kidney function tests, to monitor your progress. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions or your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized guidance regarding this medication.
